title: Marching March
subtitle: An epic composition about the countless unimportant people.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: Comrade Windsong and Comrade Raisa helped me take the children home; it took some time.

content.speaker: Knut
content.text: Comrade Evgeni once mentioned that he kept some things in the cabinet in the meeting room.

content.speaker: Knut
content.text: He said to take them out when the time was right.

content.speaker: Knut
content.text: Here. This is all of it.

trails.title: School
trails.description: This is the building that's garnered the most attention in town, where blank pages are splashed with vibrant colors.

trails.title: Dodgy Excavators
trails.description: It's only natural that minor conflicts arise during the mining process.

content.speaker: Raisa
content.text: Comrade Vila frequents this place, always looking great in her poneva dress.

content.speaker: Raisa
content.text: I taught her how to sew, and other comrades would bring piles of torn coats and socks for us to mend. This is something I have always done.

content.speaker: Raisa
content.text: No matter how catchy our slogans are, we still need clothes to wear and bread to eat, right? The rest is not within my realm of concern.

content.speaker: Raisa
content.text: Thankfully, Comrade Vila has been diligently caring for the children. My main worry was that once the teachers were gone, there would be no one to check on them and ensure they were looked after.

content.speaker: Raisa
content.text: Leaving children to run amok on the streets will not lead to their healthy development.

content.speaker: Raisa
content.text: I'm very grateful that she's here.

content.speaker: Raisa
content.text: This place has become a second home to me. Despite the challenges and endless tasks, I feel content knowing that our efforts benefit our fellow comrades.

content.speaker: Raisa
content.text: This experience is priceless to me. Anyone who has ever sat at a long table, sharing butter and conversation with people from different countries and working together to form friendships would understand the value of this way of life.

content.speaker: Raisa
content.text: It has a powerful effect, my friend. It reminds me of dark bread - rough, but filling.

content.speaker: Raisa
content.text: Whether it is Comrade Vila or ... Comrade Evgeni, I trust in their abilities. This town will not simply disappear.

content.speaker: Raisa
content.text: Rayashki will always be here, steadfast and unwavering.

trails.title: Town Square Meet-Up
trails.description: Pour out your thoughts and feelings here.

content.text:
Miners, covered in a layer of dust and wielding their picks, hurry over as others join them after washing off their bandages. In the square, some take shelter under the statue and read books, while children are led by loving hands through rows of coats and boots. A strong sense of camaraderie unites everyone in the square; they are all part of the same tight-knit community.

    The conversations begin and spread like a hurricane, sweeping from one end of the square to the other as everyone tries to engage with those around them. But then another voice joins in. The town's teacher has arrived, embodying the ideals we hold dear. She is like a character from a legend who has come to our town from a faraway place. Because of our strong will, even legends can become reality here. If the teacher had not said, "See you tomorrow!" this would have gone on all night.

    As a community, we each have a voice in shaping the future of our town. It's inspiring to see so many people come together to make a difference. There is a sense of pride that radiates from within, uniting us all towards a common goal.

    Oh, how powerful it is when we come together as one!

items.text: New Mine, Rayashki
The steel behemoths rumble.
They have plowed through snow, mud, and soil to reach their target.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I haven't done any field investigation of ley energy since our school fell apart.
Windsong puts away her tools, hands trembling slightly.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Don't worry, Comrade Windsong. Look, these stones are still the same stones we've always known.
He catches the worry in Windsong's expression.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: And don't be afraid to fail. My father told me that failure is just success in progress, hahaha!

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Even if we cannot find this new resource or save our Rayashki ...

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: We've come back here together and worked for our common goal. We have nothing to complain about.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Alright.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Whatever the result, we thank you for your efforts.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Now leave the rest to us!
He turns his head and shouts toward the drilling machine.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Comrade Yuri, check the connection status.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Don't forget to check the drill, Comrade Elena.

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: Relax. It's much easier than opening a can with only your fingers.

items.speaker: Workers
items.text: Hahahahaha!
The excited queue flows like a steady river.
People crowd together, shovels, hoes, and picks ringing out in unison.
Magnificent drilling machines emerge up from the snow.
They roar as their drills pierce the earth.
The stubborn frozen soil does nothing to hinder their progress.
Their resonance is a sound that echoes in Windsong's ears, the sound of impassioned unity of purpose and vision.
This place is like the square, like their public canteen, like their factory.
Like every corner of Rayashki.
Clearly, it is a scene worth capturing.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Knut had grown a slender arm. One that reached places no one could and picked up stones there.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: They are not like the soft, transparent stones from the sky; these are hard as chocolate!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: I think they are good stuff, too. Vila said we could make them into cans and houses to help the town!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: But maybe we will irritate the owner of the stones?
The busy adults pay no heed to the child's mutterings.
They gather around the newly collected core samples.

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: Am I right that this sample is from 100 meters underground?

items.speaker: Worker II
items.text: Yes. Usually, we don't need to reach that deep to find runium ore.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Relax, comrades. At least, it proves there is something new under Rayashki.

items.speaker: Worker II
items.text: Hmm, I have been a miner for forty years, and one thing I know for sure is this: this is not bedrock.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It's a Kikituk's hair.
Windsong carefully scrapes the colorful powder from the rocks and places it into a test tube.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The black marks are the new resource we're looking for, the red brown ones are the Kikituks, and the bright yellow ones are their mineral-eating relatives, the Hoituks.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Hmm. The machine will show us the stability of the ley energy in a minute.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: We are at the source of the ley energy now, so the lines should have been pure.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: If my eyes serve me right, I think I see bad news.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: You're right. This source is like an estuary polluted beyond recovery.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It is carrying too many traces, both from creatures and non-creatures. Besides, the "black" ore down there seems to have attracted a large number of critters, which has only worsened the pollution.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: A senior of mine said in his notes that in this case, it will take a push for the core to activate its self-purification system.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Shoot, we got a big one!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Waves! It's seawater!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: We should have prepared swimming floats.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Yes, but the waves won't reach us if we ride the sled!
There is a slight hum from the vibration.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: "If the ley energy materializes, put in a 7.62cm sea serpent bone, 3 drops of common vervain sap, and 20mg of snail sawfish embryo ..."
The Emergency Ley Energy Handling Guidelines (Trial) booklet in her hand is thrown to the ground and stamped aggressively.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Crazy! Whoa!
A colored slime continues to ooze out.
No longer a mere note in her reference materials, but an observable substance.
The clever dreamer continues his observation.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: It has a beautiful stone on its neck, too!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Did your father also fall asleep in the mine?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: D**n! Is that the raw runium ore that Zeno has been looking for? The energy is so pure. No wonder it materialized into such a huge body.
Drawn in by the spectacle, more creatures emerge from nearby mine shafts.

items.speaker: Kikituk
items.text: *roars*
Enticed by the potential for a feast.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Comrades, defense formation.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Miners, stay behind us and evacuate!

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Comrades! Stand with me if you've got a weapon! No matter if it's a rifle, a staff, or a shovel. Grip them tight. This is our Rayashki's future we're fighting for!

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: We've been waiting for this, haven't we?

items.speaker: The Other Resident
items.text: That's right.
More "weapons" are raised, clanging together as they begin their battle march.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Dear comrades.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: This is the critical moment for our town.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: No good weapons, no external support, but we have our friends, our family ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: And each other, who will never leave anyone behind!

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Yes!

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: There's nothing to be afraid of.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: We can always figure it out, so long as ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: So long as we still have hope.
Voices ring out one after another as they reach the end of their march.
The nosey critters have all disappeared, and the strange entity has slumped down.
The gathered warriors are exhausted, but alive.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Did we make it?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: After we drove the critters away, the self-purification system began to run slower.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Haha! Time to go all out. Let's go, comrades!

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: For a brighter future!
The crowd redoubles their strength as they follow Knut forward.
Deafening sounds reverberate all around them.
A brilliant red splashes across the snowfield.

items.speaker: Worker II
items.text: Oh!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Comrade Yuri! Get a few more comrades here. We need to move him to the back!
Many comrades are wounded, blood soaking their arms, but their hearts have not faltered.
Never retreat, never surrender.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Its energy has not run out yet. What on earth ...

items.speaker: Ley Energy?
items.text: *roars*

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: That's the ore! D**n it! Don't tell me it's still powering this thing!

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: I see. So we just break that stone, and it's over, right?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Yes, theoretically.
Windsong's voice wavers as she catches her breath.

items.speaker: Guard I
items.text: Leave it to me. I am the marksman here! Just need to get a little closer, a little closer.

items.speaker: Guard II
items.text: Comrade Adrian, Comrade Daniel, and I will go with you. There may be something we can do!

items.speaker: Guards
items.text: Okay!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Comrades, watch out!
They charge ahead, their spirits unwavering.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: No!

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Fall back, fall back!
Bullets fly through the air, their sound like a relentless pounding hail.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: S**t! Our attacks cannot break that stone at all.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Comrade Windsong, wh-what is going on?
The red splashes around them, so vivid against the white snow, halt her words.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The cycle of ley energy is long. It may take months, years, or even longer than that to return to its source.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: As long as that ore remains on its neck, the ley energy will continue with the purification until it wipes out everything around.
Windsong's voice is low, despite the din of battle.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: So all we can do is wait?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: For our own safety, we'd better stay out of this area until it completely returns to the source.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I should've seen this coming. I'm so sorry.
Surrounded by fallen comrades and dark red streaks, Windsong attempts to conceal the fear in her voice.
The wind rises, sharp and howling.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Comrade Patrik, Comrade Nikita, you're not done yet, right? Anyone else?

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: We still got the digger, the crane, and our own strength! Let's try harder! It's nothing more than a stupid stone! We can do this!

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: It's our last chance!
Rough hands stubbornly rise once more, defying the cold wind and danger.
Trickles of blood seep down their arms from cuts and wounds.
Warm words cover them like a bandage, offering some solace to their pain.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Stop this senseless sacrifice, Comrade Knut. It's pointless to keep going.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: But, to save Rayashki is also your dream, no?!

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Our little one from afar swore she would unite all of us, no matter who we are or where we're from.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: We must keep all that in our minds. How can we give up now?
The massive creature stands unmoving, like an unyielding mountain.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I'm so happy I came here and made friends with all of you, comrades. You each have a kind heart and a strong will.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Before I met you, my dream was only a joke to the other Rusalki, but you've shown me it isn't unreachable. Now it feels so real and heartwarming.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Sometimes, I almost forget that you see the fins and scales on my body.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: That's why I don't want you to sacrifice yourselves for nothing. I don't want to lose you.
Her smile is a ray of light breaking through the clouds.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: What we want is to stay together. That's why we are fighting to save Rayashki, right?

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: F**k this world!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: *sobs* The swans have lost their feathers.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Are we still able to reach the sky?
Snow begins to fall again, as if casting a veil over the dead—over Rayashki.
The roar of the wind grows, but there is something else groaning with it. Clouds are pushed aside, and a distorted voice calls out from above.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: I must thank you, Comrade Windsong. You've rekindled something in me, in us—a new hope, just as you promised.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: I will tell you that I read some papers on your ley lines after that night. It holds some great ideas, I admit. You and Rayashki deserve a better future.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Wow, sea swallow, our brave friend!

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Comrades, I want you to know I recommended you to Zeno only because I was worried for your future. I did not want you to be stuck in a dying town.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Comrade Evgeni?

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: And it gives me pain to see how brave and determined you all have been. I won't let any of you die here.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Evgeni, what are you doing!

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: The sad thing is I took a very different path long ago. But what does it matter now?

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Rayashki is proud of you. I am proud of you. You will continue to build the new world of your dreams—our dream, no matter where or when.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: I will always be there with you.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Seize the opportunity, Vila, Windsong, my comrades!
*boom*

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Природа это числа и черты.
The trails of the old machines wore deep into the frozen ground, forming a raised pathway that led up and away from the scene.
The children, finally coming to grips with what they've seen, begin to cry.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Comrade Evgeni.
Do fish mourn? Can a Rusalka cry?
No one can really answer this question.
Yet around the Rusalka, a ring of salty water seems to rise.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: D**n it! This is not fair!

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Just because he was the only pilot here doesn't mean he could make that decision alone! We should have had a vote!

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: We fixed that fighter together!

items.speaker: Worker I
items.text: That a*****e left us behind.

items.speaker: Worker II
items.text: But he will always be our comrade, right?
Time appears to stand still, as all present stand unmoving, unspeaking.
Until one, and then many, trembling hands rise triumphantly into the sky.

items.speaker: Residents
items.text: To Comrade Evgeni, salute!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: But where is the sea swallow?!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: He flew into the future, child.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: The future we'll all reach one day.
